Risks.riskTitle: Sprint 1 delivery delay from scope expansion and client cloud dependency
Risks.riskDescription: Broader scope and client cloud environment dependencies caused Sprint 1 delivery to slip by one week, reducing the customer validation window and creating risk to subsequent sprint timelines.

riskChain.rootCause: Broader-than-planned scope combined with dependency on client cloud environment readiness.
riskChain.trigger: Sprint work or environment dependency is not completed within the planned sprint window.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Sprint delivery slips and customer validation time is compressed.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Subsequent sprint activities become more schedule-sensitive and may inherit delay, carryover, or rework pressure.
riskChain.impact: Execution sequencing and overall schedule reliability weaken.

Risks.businessImpact: The one-week slip already reduced the validation window. In the current project context, compressed validation can delay acceptance feedback, increase rework carryover, and reduce schedule resilience for subsequent sprint commitments.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: From vivli Risk dump.xlsx: 'Sprint 1 delivery slipped by one week due to broader scope and client cloud environment dependencies' and 'Reduced customer validation window and potential impact to subsequent sprint timelines.'
Risks.currentContextReasoning: The project is in active execution and historically exposed to dependency-led schedule pressure. Scope expansion and client-controlled environment readiness create a direct path from delivery slip to compressed validation and downstream schedule strain.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical cluster 12077-CL-001 documents sprint delivery dependency and schedule slippage caused by broader scope and client cloud environment dependency.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: The current risk directly matches the historical project record in the same project, including cause, event, and downstream effect.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If scope growth or client environment readiness issues recur in later execution windows, the most likely next effect is additional validation compression and downstream sprint carryover.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Although the dataset contains one occurrence, it is directly from the same project and exactly aligns to the present risk pattern.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Environment access delays, unresolved client-side cloud actions, sprint work still open near sprint end, reduced validation duration, increased carryover backlog.
Risks.predictiveInsight: This risk is most likely to evolve into broader schedule instability when scope expansion and external dependency latency occur together.
Risks.mitigation: Enforce sprint-entry dependency readiness checks for client cloud access, freeze sprint scope after planning, and escalate any environment blocker through the defined weekly governance cadence before it affects validation dates.
Risks.recommendations: 1. Add a pre-sprint dependency checkpoint for all client environment prerequisites. 2. Require explicit approval for any in-sprint scope addition. 3. Protect customer validation time by moving dependency-risk review to the start and midpoint of each sprint. 4. Track compressed validation as a formal leading indicator in weekly status review.

Risks.riskTitle: Post-initiation additions outside SOW create scope and effort exposure
Risks.riskDescription: Regression testing and extended PAT duration were added after project initiation and are not part of the original SOW, creating scope creep, contractual ambiguity, and unplanned effort risk.

riskChain.rootCause: Testing and PAT obligations expanded after initiation without SOW baseline alignment.
riskChain.trigger: Additional test and validation work is expected without formal scope, commercial, or timeline adjustment.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Project effort expands beyond baseline assumptions and governance control weakens.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Unplanned work consumes sprint capacity, contributes to schedule slippage, and may create acceptance or payment ambiguity.
riskChain.impact: Scope control, commercial clarity, and execution predictability are degraded.

Risks.businessImpact: This risk can drive unplanned effort, reduce available capacity for committed sprint work, and create contractual ambiguity around included obligations and delivery acceptance.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: From vivli Risk dump.xlsx: 'Regression testing and extended PAT duration were added after project initiation but are not part of the original SOW' and 'Potential scope creep, contractual ambiguity, and unplanned effort.'
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This is an upstream governance risk. In a phased sprint delivery model, additions to regression and PAT do not remain administrative issues; they consume execution capacity and can trigger downstream schedule pressure.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical cluster 12077-CL-002 documents scope expansion and SOW misalignment after project initiation.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: The current risk directly reflects the same historical project pattern: post-initiation additions, contractual ambiguity, and unplanned effort.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If testing obligations continue to expand without formal change control, the project will likely experience capacity erosion, milestone tension, and further delivery compression.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: This exact issue is historically evidenced in the same project and is a known governance failure mode in the available intelligence.
Risks.leadingIndicators: PAT duration increases, regression tasks added without approval, backlog growth from enhancements, disputes on what is in scope, rising effort without revised baseline.
Risks.predictiveInsight: This is the most important upstream risk in the set because it can propagate into both schedule and validation risk.
Risks.mitigation: Apply formal change control for all added testing obligations, restate acceptance criteria and delivery boundaries, and align effort, timeline, and commercial treatment before absorbing additional work.
Risks.recommendations: 1. Produce an SOW variance log for regression, PAT, and test obligations. 2. Route all additions through monthly PMR and weekly status governance until baseline is reset. 3. Reconfirm acceptance criteria for testing-related deliverables with Vivli. 4. Prevent added validation tasks from entering active sprint execution without sponsor approval.

Risks.riskTitle: Delayed customer feedback may disrupt validation and implementation
Risks.riskDescription: Customer feedback is expected by 20 July, and any delay could interrupt subsequent sprint validation and implementation activities.

riskChain.rootCause: Reliance on timely customer feedback within a tightly sequenced validation process.
riskChain.trigger: Expected customer feedback or approval is not received within the needed decision window.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Validation activities cannot proceed as planned.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Implementation sequencing, sprint acceptance, and dependent delivery commitments become compressed or postponed.
riskChain.impact: Schedule confidence declines and carryover or rework exposure increases.

Risks.businessImpact: Delayed client feedback can defer validation closure, postpone implementation decisions, and compress time available to address issues before the next execution milestone.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: From vivli Risk dump.xlsx: 'Customer feedback is expected by 20 July. Any delay may impact subsequent sprint validation and implementation.'
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This project is dependent on client review and response timing. In the historical record, customer responsiveness is a direct execution bottleneck rather than a secondary issue.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical cluster 12077-CL-003 documents client feedback delay impact on sprint validation and implementation sequencing.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: The current risk directly mirrors the historical issue in the same project, including the dependency chain from delayed feedback to validation disruption.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If business review or approval latency continues, later execution stages will become more schedule-sensitive, especially where fixed validation and implementation windows depend on client turnaround.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: This pattern is directly evidenced in the same project and is also reinforced by portfolio observations that approval latency is a recurring bottleneck.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Missed feedback dates, unresolved review items, delayed approval responses, growing client-owned action list, validation tasks waiting on business confirmation.
Risks.predictiveInsight: This dependency becomes most dangerous after any prior sprint delay because compressed timelines reduce tolerance for customer response latency.
Risks.mitigation: Set explicit feedback turnaround commitments, pre-book review sessions before deliverable handoff, and escalate delayed client responses through named governance contacts when decision windows are missed.
Risks.recommendations: 1. Tie customer review dates to sprint exit criteria. 2. Use the agreed escalation contacts when feedback is late beyond the accepted window. 3. Present pending client decisions separately in weekly review to avoid hidden schedule erosion. 4. Sequence validation work so client-dependent items are surfaced as early as possible.

majorBottlenecks: Post-initiation scope expansion affecting testing obligations
riskPropagationPatterns: SOW/scope ambiguity -> broader execution scope -> sprint delay -> compressed validation -> downstream schedule sensitivity
Client environment dependency -> execution delay -> reduced validation window -> greater impact from feedback latency
Customer feedback delay -> blocked validation -> postponed implementation sequencing
emergingConcerns: Reactive surfacing of risks during delivery rather than fully during pre-execution planning
Weak operational metadata quality limiting measured learning from historical closures
highRiskDependencies: Testing obligations not fully bounded in original SOW
rootCauseConcentration: External dependency on client environment and customer inputs
Planning precision and effort estimation gap
mostLikelyFailureTriggers: Expansion of PAT/regression demand without change control
projectForecastInsights.overallOutlook: Cautious. Historical evidence indicates that this project's primary exposure is not technical failure but delivery-governance strain: scope ambiguity, client dependencies, and feedback latency. If governance controls are strengthened early, the risk chain is containable; if not, downstream schedule pressure is likely to recur.

Risks.riskTitle: Schedule remains at risk during active Sprint 4 delivery
Risks.riskDescription: Sprint 4 solution development and QA validation are still in progress while the project schedule status is under review, which may affect planned completion of Sprint 4 and readiness for Sprint 5 activities.

riskChain.rootCause: Active Sprint 4 development and QA remain open close to target completion while overall schedule is under review.
riskChain.trigger: Sprint 4 work is not completed by planned target dates for demo and verification.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Sprint 4 completion slips or exits with unresolved work.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Sprint 5 start, demo timing, PAT preparation, and later release windows are compressed.
riskChain.impact: Remaining lifecycle schedule resilience is reduced.

Risks.businessImpact: Delay in Sprint 4 can directly affect Sprint 5 readiness, user demo timing, PAT entry, regression period, and deployment preparation for both use cases.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: From Vivli_Project_Weekly_Review__Session_0813_V1.0.pptx: 'The Sprint 4 solution development and QA validation is currently in progress – 08/14'; schedule status is 'UNDER REVIEW'; Sprint 4 Demo and PAT - Early Access Review are 'Yet to Start'; complete Sprint 4 to Vivli Cloud QA3 for demo and verification was targeted for 08/14.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This risk is directly evidenced by active execution status. The timeline is tightly sequenced from Sprint 4 into Sprint 5, user demo, PAT, regression, go-live, training, and hypercare, so any current slip propagates quickly.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical Vivli evidence shows sprint delay caused by scope and dependency issues led to reduced validation window and downstream timeline pressure.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: The historical project is different in formal naming, but same client evidence shows a similar schedule propagation pattern: execution disruption -> compressed validation -> subsequent timeline risk.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If Sprint 4 does not close cleanly, the project is likely to carry unresolved development, QA, or PAT feedback into Sprint 5, reducing capacity for planned Sprint 5 work.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Current evidence is strong. Historical enrichment is moderate because the same client has already shown similar execution-to-validation schedule compression.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Sprint 4 work open after target date, demo movement beyond 08/17, unresolved code review actions, growing bug backlog, repeated 'under review' schedule status.
Risks.predictiveInsight: The strongest early warning is not just late completion, but unfinished QA and unresolved feedback persisting into the demo window.
Risks.mitigation: Create a Sprint 4 closure war room with daily review of remaining development, QA, review comments, and PAT observation closure until all sprint exit criteria are met.
Risks.recommendations: 1. Separate must-close Sprint 4 items from carryover candidates immediately. 2. Freeze nonessential Sprint 5 intake until Sprint 4 exit risk is reduced. 3. Escalate any client-side blockers using the documented service and escalation managers. 4. Re-baseline short-term milestone dates if closure confidence drops further.

Risks.riskTitle: Pending escalation requirement refinement may delay chat solution progress
Risks.riskDescription: Chat-based escalation requirements are still pending discussion, which may delay requirement finalization and affect delivery progress for the Agentic Chat workstream.

riskChain.rootCause: Unresolved chat-based escalation requirements pending client-side discussion.
riskChain.trigger: Implementation work needs decisions that are not finalized in time.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Agentic Chat design or build progress is delayed or proceeds on assumptions.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Rework, backlog carryover, or incomplete sprint deliverables affect later validation and acceptance.
riskChain.impact: Chat workstream delivery certainty is reduced.

Risks.businessImpact: Escalation to a human team member is part of the committed chatbot deliverable. If requirements remain open, core workflow completion, testing, and acceptance of the Agentic Chat use case may be delayed.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: From weekly review dependency list: 'Refine chat-based escalation requirements (pending Amruta-Sarah discussion).' Sprint 5 plans include 'Integrate the escalation workflow through chat-based notifications.' From SOW: 'Escalation path to a human client’s team member for complex or sensitive queries.'
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This is a direct dependency on a defined deliverable, not an optional enhancement. The requirement is still open while the implementation plan already assumes integration work in the next sprint.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical Vivli evidence shows unresolved scope and client-input dependencies created schedule and governance strain.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: No exact historical chat-escalation analogue exists, but the same client shows a consistent pattern where unresolved scope and client response dependencies create downstream delivery pressure.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If the requirement discussion remains unresolved, the likely result is assumption-based design, deferred implementation, or rework during demo and PAT.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Moderate. The exact feature is new, but the dependency pattern is historically consistent for Vivli work.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Requirement discussion not completed before sprint build tasks, missing acceptance criteria, blocked stories, provisional design notes, demo exclusions for escalation flow.
Risks.predictiveInsight: This risk is likely to escalate quietly until dependent build or test steps fail to progress, so decision latency should be monitored as closely as development progress.
Risks.mitigation: Time-box the pending business discussion, convert outcomes into approved acceptance criteria, and prevent further escalation-workflow build from proceeding on undocumented assumptions.
Risks.recommendations: 1. Set a hard decision deadline before Sprint 5 build execution. 2. Record agreed escalation workflow, trigger conditions, and ownership in the sprint backlog. 3. If unresolved, isolate the feature behind a controlled scope boundary rather than allowing hidden rework. 4. Review the requirement outcome in the next weekly status review.

Risks.riskTitle: Pending monitoring and dead-letter queue decisions may weaken operational readiness
Risks.riskDescription: Confirmation of the Azure monitoring and escalation email failure alert process is still pending and Vivli must complete the dead-letter queue story internally, which may delay operational readiness for the solution.

riskChain.rootCause: Operational monitoring and failure-handling decisions remain unresolved and partly client-owned.
riskChain.trigger: Monitoring, alerting, or failure-management controls are not finalized before deployment readiness activities.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Solution reaches later validation or deployment stages without complete operational controls.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Go-live approval is delayed or service enters production with weak observability and recovery readiness.
riskChain.impact: Operational readiness and deployment confidence are reduced.

Risks.businessImpact: This may delay deployment readiness, weaken production support posture, and increase incident-detection and triage risk after go-live.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: From weekly review dependency list: 'Confirm Azure monitoring and escalation email failure alert process. Vivli to do the story internally for dead-letter queue.' From SOW deployment milestone: 'Production deployment completed; smoke testing validated; go-live approval received; production monitoring initiated.'
Risks.currentContextReasoning: The dependency is directly tied to contractual deployment readiness and is client-controlled in part, making late resolution a realistic blocker.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical Vivli evidence shows client-controlled external dependencies have previously created execution and validation timing risk.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: There is no direct historical monitoring-readiness example, only a broader client-dependency pattern.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If monitoring and dead-letter queue decisions remain unresolved, operational readiness could become a late-stage gate and delay deployment or force a weaker go-live posture.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Weak-to-moderate. The specific risk is new, but the underlying client-readiness dependency pattern is historically supported.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Open client-owned DLQ story, undefined alert routing, no runbook approval, deferred monitoring design sign-off, deployment checklist gaps.
Risks.predictiveInsight: This risk often surfaces late; without early action, the project may appear functionally ready while still failing operational readiness checks.
Risks.mitigation: Define a minimum operational readiness baseline now covering monitoring, alerting, failure routing, and dead-letter handling, and assign decision dates to client-owned items.
Risks.recommendations: 1. Move this dependency into the formal RAID review each week until closed. 2. Create a go-live readiness checklist tied to the SOW deployment milestone. 3. Obtain written ownership and due date for the Vivli internal DLQ story. 4. Do not defer observability decisions into hypercare.

Risks.riskTitle: Lack of dedicated automation testing environment may constrain validation
Risks.riskDescription: A dedicated automation testing environment still needs to be provisioned, which may limit test execution readiness and affect validation activities for the project.

riskChain.rootCause: Dedicated automation testing environment is not yet fully available.
riskChain.trigger: Automation testing cannot run when validation volume and timing require it.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Validation coverage is reduced or delayed.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Manual testing reliance increases, defects are found later, and PAT or regression windows compress.
riskChain.impact: Quality assurance efficiency and release confidence are weakened.

Risks.businessImpact: Without timely automation environment readiness, the project may rely too heavily on manual validation despite growing rule complexity, increasing both schedule pressure and defect escape risk.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: From weekly review dependency list: 'Provision dedicated automation testing environment.' From Project Risks & Issues slide: 'risk of relying heavily on manual validation given the growing number of form validation rules'; 'Extensive backend automated testing is already in place'; 'The automation resource has been mobilized. The resource starts in the 4th sprint.'
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This is an immediate current-state risk because validation complexity is growing while the enabling environment is still pending. The project is already in Sprint 4 and moving toward PAT and regression windows.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical Vivli evidence shows environment dependencies contributed to sprint delay and reduced validation windows.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: While the exact environment differs, the same causal pattern is present: environment readiness dependency -> test/delivery delay -> compressed downstream validation.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If the environment is not provisioned soon, automated coverage will lag and defects may be discovered later in PAT or regression when the schedule is less flexible.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Moderate historical support plus strong current evidence make this one of the most credible forward-looking risks.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Automation scripts blocked, rising manual test effort, UI coverage lagging backend coverage, defects surfacing late, regression backlog increasing.
Risks.predictiveInsight: The true escalation signal is not only delayed provisioning, but delayed usability of the environment early enough to absorb defects before PAT.
Risks.mitigation: Fast-track environment provisioning, validate toolchain usability immediately after provision, and prioritize the highest-risk automated scenarios for form validation and UI flows.
Risks.recommendations: 1. Assign a named owner and due date for full environment readiness. 2. Run a short proof-of-execution to confirm the environment is usable, not merely provisioned. 3. Prioritize automation for high-volume rule validation and UI regression paths. 4. Track manual-to-automated test ratio weekly until the risk is reduced.

Risks.riskTitle: Pending Guru Card fit assessment may delay Agentic Chat decisions
Risks.riskDescription: The Guru Card fit assessment for Agentic chat remains open, which may delay design or implementation decisions for the chat solution.

riskChain.rootCause: Required fit assessment for Guru Card remains unresolved.
riskChain.trigger: Design or implementation decisions need the assessment outcome before work can proceed confidently.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Agentic Chat workstream decisions are delayed or proceed provisionally.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Features may be deferred, redesigned, or validated late, causing carryover into later sprint work.
riskChain.impact: Chat solution predictability and design stability are reduced.

Risks.businessImpact: If Guru Card is materially tied to chat capability design, delayed resolution can affect solution direction and create rework. However, the exact criticality is not fully defined in the available artifacts.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: From weekly review dependency list: 'Get Guru Card fit assessment in Agentic chat.' The project artifacts do not provide additional detail on whether this is mandatory for baseline delivery or an optional design path.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: The risk is valid because it is an active open dependency, but evidence on its exact business criticality is limited compared with other project risks.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical Vivli evidence generally shows unresolved dependencies can affect downstream timing.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: There is no direct historical analogue for Guru Card in the provided evidence.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If the assessment remains open into implementation or validation, design decisions may be delayed or revised late, affecting planned chat feature progress.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Weak historical support; the risk is mainly supported by current open dependency evidence.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Assessment still open with no target resolution, blocked design decisions, provisional feature scope, re-estimation after dependency outcome.
Risks.predictiveInsight: The impact could escalate quickly if Guru Card turns out to be central to the chat design path, so this dependency should not be allowed to drift without an explicit business decision.
Risks.mitigation: Clarify whether Guru Card is a must-have, should-have, or exploratory dependency for the current release and align sprint planning accordingly.
Risks.recommendations: 1. Force a business/technical decision on release criticality. 2. If noncritical, decouple it from near-term sprint commitments. 3. If critical, assign an approval deadline and dependency owner. 4. Reflect the decision explicitly in Sprint 5 planning and demo scope.

projectForecastInsights.overallOutlook: Guarded but manageable. Scope and cost are reported on track, but schedule is already under review and several active dependencies are positioned to affect validation, Sprint 5 execution, and deployment readiness. The project can remain recoverable if decision latency, environment readiness, and operational controls are closed quickly and governed weekly.
